title: 分形与自相似 · Day 17 — Mathematics

questions.question: 测量海岸线时，尺子从 100 公里换到 1 公里，测出的长度越来越大且没有极限。对此最恰当的理解是什么？
options: 海岸线实际上是二维图形，应该测它的面积而不是长度
海岸线没有确定长度，应改用分形维数刻画它的粗糙程度
这是测量误差不断累积造成的，只要换用更精密的仪器重新测量就能消除
只要尺子足够短，测出的长度最终会收敛到一个真实值
questions.explanation: 尺子越短测得越长且趋于无穷，说明海岸线介于一维的线和二维的面之间，「多长」这个问题本身不成立；该量的是它的分形维数（约 1.25）。它比直线更密，但没铺满平面，所以也不是二维的面。
questions.question_en: Measuring a coastline with rulers shrinking from 100 km to 1 km yields ever larger lengths with no limit. What is the best way to understand this?
options_en: A coastline is really a two-dimensional shape, so we should measure its area rather than its length
A coastline has no definite length; its roughness should be described with a fractal dimension instead
It comes from accumulated measurement error, which remeasuring with more precise instruments would remove
With a short enough ruler, the measured length eventually converges to a true value
questions.explanation_en: Shorter rulers give longer lengths without bound, showing the coastline sits between a one-dimensional line and a two-dimensional surface, so "how long is it" has no answer. What should be measured is its fractal dimension, about 1.25; it is denser than a line but doesn't fill the plane, so it isn't a surface either.

questions.question: 某个自相似图形，按 1/3 的比例缩小后，需要 4 个副本才能拼回原图。按盒计数的思路，它的维数是多少？
options: 2，因为它由多个副本拼成，铺满了一块平面
questions.explanation: 维数 D 满足「副本数 = (1/缩放比)^D」，即 4 = 3^D，所以 D = log 4 / log 3 ≈ 1.26，这正是科赫曲线。正方形减半需 4 = 2^2 个副本得 D = 2，同样是对数之比而不是简单相除。
questions.question_en: A self-similar figure, when scaled down by a factor of 1/3, needs 4 copies to reassemble the original. By box-counting reasoning, what is its dimension?
options_en: 2, because it is tiled from multiple copies that cover a patch of the plane
questions.explanation_en: The dimension D satisfies copies = (1/scale)^D, so 4 = 3^D and D = log 4 / log 3 ≈ 1.26, which is the Koch curve. A square halved needs 4 = 2^2 copies, giving D = 2; it is a ratio of logarithms, not a simple quotient.

questions.question: 一组数据在双对数坐标上大致排成一条直线，研究者据此宣布它服从幂律、是无标度的分形现象。按文中的提醒，问题在哪？
options: 双对数坐标上的直线意味着指数分布，恰好与幂律相反
直线的斜率必须是整数，才能算作分形维数
幂律只会出现在数学构造里，自然界里真实测得的数据不可能服从幂律分布
双对数图上像直线不等于幂律，对数正态分布也很像
questions.explanation: 幂律在双对数坐标上确实是直线，斜率就是维数，但反过来不成立：对数正态分布在这种坐标下也很像直线，这是经典的统计陷阱。自然界的统计自相似（河网、地震、城市规模）恰恰常用幂律刻画，斜率也可以是分数。
questions.question_en: A dataset falls roughly on a straight line in log-log coordinates, and a researcher declares it a scale-free power law. Per the caution in the text, what is wrong?
options_en: A straight line on log-log axes indicates an exponential distribution, the opposite of a power law
The slope must be an integer before it can count as a fractal dimension
Power laws occur only in mathematical constructions; real measured data in nature can never follow one
Looking straight on a log-log plot doesn't prove a power law; a lognormal looks similar
questions.explanation_en: A power law does appear as a straight line on log-log axes, with the slope giving the dimension, but the converse fails: lognormal distributions can look nearly straight too, a classic statistical trap. Statistical self-similarity in nature, from river networks to earthquakes and city sizes, is in fact commonly described by power laws, and the slope can be fractional.
